Stepanov considered his options. Either he was to give in and perhaps lose his life in a Siberian prison, or he was to stand in defiance of Valenteev. And if he stood in defiance, who knew what lay in store? So he picked up the phone and stood in defiance.

Velenteev heard the phone ring and his heart skipped. Could this be it? The moment where for once, they won? They could stop fighting and pushing and rest. Rest, for once, no more stressing about statism or despots or death in the name of life. Just rest. He picked up the phone and his heart skipped again.

He wasn't prepared for this response. He hadn't thought he would be called on his bluff. He didn't have the men, the money, to fight a war. God, how could he be so stupid? Those next words from Stepanov ripped the man's heart out, his idealism, his hope.
strings.SBA_Despotist.11.a:
“How about we forget about this,
and you retire to your dacha.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.12.desc:
It all came down to these next few moments. Years of waiting, planning, preparing, of putting up with Siuda's “Comrade” nonsense, of selecting the right soldiers, even making sure the weather was right, Stepanov had to call this off twice already because of rain.. But the weather had held up today and the General Assembly was crowded. It had to be today or it would never happen.

“Comrade Stepanov, you still have not explained what happened to Comrade Pyotr Siuda. He was under your protection, his disappearance has concerned a great many in this Assembly.” The words snapped Stepanov back to reality, as he stared at the many faces of the Assembly, all staring back at him intently, waiting for an answer. He looked at his notes, a long speech decrying Pyotr, pointing out his many failures and general lack of intelligence. Claiming his 'disappearance' was that overzealous child's own fault. But that wasn't Stepanov's style, it never had been. “Comrades.” Stepanov grinned as that hated term caused a sea of disgust among those in the Assembly “I don't have to answer for the tragic fate of comrade Pyotr. Because as of this moment, this Assembly is disbanded.” He pressed a button hidden underneath the podium.

“Comrade Stepanov, what is this statist madness?” An assemblyman asked right before dozens of members of the Black Army poured into the room. A wave of relief hit Stepanov as he gripped the podium. This was a moment he had pictured for so long, part of him had never believed it would happen. And yet here it was.

One of the assemblymen rose to his feet “This is a betrayal, Stepanov! Of the Free Territory and all-” One of the soldiers dragged him back down to his seat, securing his silence with the butt of her rifle. Stepanov grabbed the microphone. “It is regretful that such drastic actions have become necessary.” He lied “But the General Assembly has constantly shown itself incapable of managing the Free Territory. The Security Council will do just fine without you. Now if you'll cooperate with these soldiers as they escort you out of the room, we can help ensure this transition is peaceful and orderly.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.12.a: “Failure to cooperate would be inadvisable, comrade.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.13.desc:
Life was never perfect. It was hard, toiling, deadly, and most of all, short. But in Siberia, in those wastes, it was a step closer to perfect. The work was difficult, mucking barns and sowing seeds. Out there, though, it was beautiful. It never ceased being beautiful. The slow, meandering delta. The chilly wind on a summer morning, the biting cold in the winter. The snow capped mountains just peeking over the horizon. Every day was rich, unchanging, blowing like the wind. He could live like this forever.

They came at night, in a big, rumbling military truck. They rolled right up to the door and in their big boots marched to it and started knocking. It never stopped knocking. He could hear it still today. Then they pushed the door down and pulled him away. He screamed. He was only a boy. He wasn't ready to die for his country. And his mother screamed. His father tried to fight back, for a few minutes, but a gun butt to the face silenced him. They had to drag him out of the house, kicking and screaming for his life. They threw him into the back of the truck. He couldn't stop crying, with the blindfold over his head. He cried and cried and cried, always hearing that knocking. Was it even there anymore? Eventually, life faded to sleep, and dream.
strings.SBA_Despotist.13.a: He dreamed of that knocking, and his mother's scream.
strings.SBA_Despotist.14.desc:
When the boy woke up, the truck had came to a stop, and dawn broke. Two men pulled him out of the truck.

“You want to join the army, huh?”

“N-no. I just want to go home, sir. Please, I just want to go home.”

“Too fucking bad. Take this bag and get started down that valley. We'll be on the other side.”

The two of them laughed. They both knew he wouldn't make it. They headed back into the van and drove off, leaving the boy in the dust, his tears still drying. Rummaging through the bag, he found a canteen full of water, some meager rations, stale bread, and a tarp, presumably for shelter. It would have to do. What else was he to do? Wait for the vultures to take him? So he set off, kicking rocks and yelping down the trail.

When his anger finally melted into sadness, he began to look around him. The landscape reminded him of home. There wasn't a delta, but there were those same low mountains, those hills spotted with patches of trees. It almost felt like home.

He was tired, and hungry, and he had run out of bread. By now, the moon had come out. They were right. He would never make it. He hastily tied the tarp between two trees and sat down on a log, looking at the dark landscape. He never slept, just sitting there, crying, enraged and in a horrible stupor.

Until the sky began to move. It started out with a few blazes of light, but within a few minutes it had begun to vibrate and jostle with fantastic color. Green, purple, blue, lighting up the sky. Like some great indescribable dance.

“Oh, my God. They don't have this in the south.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.14.a: There he sat, the colors reflected in his tearful eyes.
strings.SBA_Despotist.15.desc:
The new Novosibirsk technical school had been nothing but trouble. The schooling was leaving kids with no idea how to do anything technical, and it seemed that the teachers were all subversives educating their pupils on nothing but anarchist revolutionary thought. Some of the students had recently been getting drunk and running an organization called the “New Anarchists”, proclaiming their hatred for the Security Council and their wish for a return to Pyotr's idealism.

It was on one freezing night in Novosibirsk when a band of the New Anarchists staged a “protest” on the street. They yelled drunken slurs at passing soldiers and threw loose bricks and rocks from the cobblestone. A crowd began to build up, of curious spectators and disgruntled soldiers. It seemed as if this was about to turn into a one-sided fight, a Boston Massacre for a new Russia. Which new Paul Revere would depict it, famously? Which Crispus Attucks would lead the charge for freedom and Anarchy?

A soldier pulled out a rusty revolver and shot it in the air three times. Perhaps the bravery of these anarchists had been overstated. Upon hearing the gunshots, they scrambled to run.
strings.SBA_Despotist.15.a: A bunch of drunken students, that is all.
strings.SBA_Despotist.16.desc:
It felt good to win. It felt good to be himself. It felt good to relax and unwind, simply sipping the most luxury alcohol Russia had to offer. Looking out from his balcony, Ivan Stepanov saw Russia, HIS Russia. Of course it 'belonged to the people', anarchy was alive and well. A matter of fact, anarchy had never been stronger! Stepanov nearly spat out his wine in laughter.

He was out there somewhere, in a shallow grave, buried in the place he loved. Poetic. Stepanov should try poetry maybe! If only he had the time in between managing people and the military. He might write down his ideas one day, who knows? A better question, who cares? Stepanov certainly didn't. This night was his alone. No Pyotr to pester him with ideology, no Valenteev to threaten his rule, and no guilt to haunt him.

General Ivan Stepanov carefully selected a record off his shelf and put it under the needle. The sun began to set over Siberia, casting a golden light on the treacherous general. Was it worth it? To put up with all the nonsense of Comrade this and that? To slaughter men in the name of an ideology he couldn't care less for? Most definitely.

Stepanov sat in his reclining chair, there would be issues: the impending liberation, the growing Black Army, weeding out the last holdouts of Pyotr's supporters. Those were issues for tomorrow. Tonight belonged to him, Russia belonged to him, the most brilliant thief, the one who stole the anarchist movement out from underneath them.
strings.SBA_Despotist.17.desc:
The revelation came at night.

Stepanov was having one of his parties, surrounded by prostitutes. A disk was playing, some old Russian hits from the union days. They were drinking and stripping; it was a normal night. That was, until she said those words.

“Oh yeah, totally nuked the trees.”

One of the prettier whores, with bright red lipstick and a short skirt that Stepanov had personally requested.

“Wait. Aleksadrina, was it? No. Karine. What did you just say?”

“I- I just said I had to cut down these trees outside of my place. One of them was going to fall. I didn't mean any offense, Mr. Stepanov. And - it's Anastasia, sir.”

“No. Karine, you used a very specific word to describe you cutting down those trees.”

“Nuked?”

“Yes. Yes, that's it! That's it!”

The Siberian hookers looked in awe as Stepanov jaunted out of the dacha, hopped into his car, and drove south. Well, he had paid them for the night and there was alcohol, why not party a little longer?

Stepanov was a little drunk, but it was clear. He needed a nuclear bomb. It was the only way. At this stage, who wouldn't invade them? Without that great deterrent which kept the rest of the world in a stasis, it would already be engulfed in war.
strings.SBA_Despotist.17.b: I hear there is much in the east!
strings.SBA_Despotist.18.desc:
Pyotr Siuda sat alone with a glass of vodka and tapped his foot. Deep in thought, he continued tapping until he realized the thump he was making. Forcing himself to breath and slow down, he realized what must be done.

The Black Army had become rulers, and if there was anything Pyotr hated more than the state, it was the rulers that upheld the state that deserved to be punished. When a people's army loses its ideals and the support of its people it simply becomes a group of bandits, and Siuda was sad to admit that that is what it had become. Who knew what they were plotting? To overthrow the anarchy, the freedom that they had fought so hard for? Restore some state rooted in the ideas of communism but so devoid of the actual ideals it represents? It must end. They must be killed. And if they couldn't be killed, worked nearly to death.

The reprisals started out small. Communes recalling soldiers or generals under “suggestion” from Pyotr. A few in the lower ranks disappeared into the north. By the end of the month, the writing was on the wall. So many men simply gone. Officially, many had simply never existed, wiped off the record. But it was an open secret where they were. Either lost to an eternal dreamless sleep, or toiling in camps up north. Life was brutal and often short in those camps. Men arrived in tears, begging for some other punishment, something else. But Siuda had enough with tyrants. He'd had enough with the people being little more than slaves of bandits. The Black Army must be cleansed.
strings.SBA_Despotist.19.desc:
It was the Jews. It must be. Who else in their right mind would take a man like him - someone fighting for the white race, for the integrity of the Aryan people - and make him mine for some god-forsaken metal? They were pulling the strings on it all. The fucking Jews.

Artur tried to determine what the smell in the mine was. Sickly, almost. But when he inhaled the air, his throat filled with thick, choking dust. He could hardly breath. God, why hadn't he fought the Jews to the death? He had killed one, he thought, but now that he thought back to it, that might have been one of his own men. The rifles. They were made my Jews, they had faulty triggers. And now what, they were making a nuclear bomb? No shit, considering atoms were a Jewish science. He had to get back to Germania. He had to warn Hitler. Was Hitler even alive anymore? Oh my God, he couldn't breathe. He had to get back to Hitler. Get out of the mine, tell him they were building a bomb. The Jews. Yes, that was it. They were building a bomb. Artur clawed his way back to the sunlight. It was that direction, wasn't it? He thought he had taken a left there... maybe it was right? Yes, there it is. The sunlight. They made these mines so dusty and dark and confusing. Maybe it was the dust. He just couldn't get the dust out.

The guard watched as a man stumbled out of the mine, wheezing and mumbling. He just kept coughing out dust.

“Get back in there, fascist scum! Your workday isn't over yet!”

The man stared back and started murmuring. “You're a Jew.” He crawled up to the guard. “Why the fuck are you sons of Zion building the bomb? Why? Answer me!” The man stopped to wheeze.

“Touch me and I'll shoot, Nazi.”

Artur limply punched the guard, and in one shot to the chest his life was gone.
strings.SBA_Despotist.19.a: Hitler never learned of the bomb.
strings.SBA_Despotist.20.desc:
Foreign media proclaimed the news in medium-sized lettering on the back of the third page.

RUSSIAN WARLORD, STEPANOV, DEVELOPS NUCLEAR BOMB

ANARCHISTS OF RUSSIA REVEAL NUCLEAR WEAPONS

Most thought it was probably just a rumor and moved on in their day. For Stepanov, it was one of his peaks. Parading the bomb through Novosibirsk - even if it was just a dummy - proved to be a truly prideful moment for Stepanov. After the large papier mache bomb was driven through Novosibirsk, he stood up on a podium in Anarchy Square and began speaking to a cold and thoroughly bored crowd.

“I wanted to thank all of the nuclear scientists that aided in the development of this technological marvel and have come here to witness its display.”

None of the scientists had shown up, but a light smattering of applause did begin. Stepanov continued. “This bomb will not only ensure our freedom, but will let our advanced capabilities be known to the entire world!”

Dick closed the newspaper. What a strange speech from Russia. Not that it concerned him. It seemed like real important news never really traveled from there all the way to America. Work began soon.
strings.SBA_Despotist.20.a: And he hadn't even had his coffee!
strings.SBA_Despotist.21.desc:
At the end of an uneventful speech, Stepanov inserted an impromptu message.

“There are many fools out there on this varied and diverse Earth. Unfortunately the original fool happened to be a sweet-talker, and so we are left with a world full of them. One particular type of fool which I despise the most is those that have faith in human nature. There is one thing to have faith in, and that is God. Not some myth of a pure man, or socialism, but the unity of god. And it seems that it is that faith that has led us to traitors, false shepherds like our old friend Siuda.

Men of Novosibirsk, do not follow in the footsteps of these men. Human nature is a terrible, terrible thing. Anarchy is nasty, brutish, and short. Only the leadership of a strongman may stop man from descending into war of all against all. I implore you, men of little faith, to rest that faith in me. For The Black Army will never stop to descend you from the tides of wild, ravaging savages. We are the new bastion of civilization in Siberia, and there is no one who will take that title away from us.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.22.desc:
The last real propaganda that Fyodor had seen were ones from the Bukharin days. Those damn posters, proclaiming the imminent defeat of the Germans and the triumphant Red Army marching forward. They used to be everywhere, plastered on every wall, smashed between every door. Now, they fluttered in the streets, stuck on trees or burned for warmth. Those unlucky enough to be stuck outside for the night stacked them on as blankets against the Siberian night. Fyodor reminisced to the days when a few unlucky posters ended up as toilet paper. They supposed that it was better than leaves.

It was strange, then, to see a new poster in Novosibirsk. This was not in the crisp red that Bukharin's poster had. With a closer look, Fyodor could see the imperfections in the printing. Color bled over lines, figures in the background were hardly more than black smudges. It was crude, but nevertheless a propaganda poster. What it depicted was strange. In the center was a man on his knees, bowing his head forward. The tattered cavalryman's uniform and wide handlebar mustache revealed the man's identity; Semyon Budyonny, that Bolshevik killed during the charge on Boguchany. With a sword to his throat was another man whose face wasn't revealed, but he had the build of a typical Black Army soldier. Squinting at the details, Fyodor could not make out the man's identity.

Fyodor has been there, at the charge. The high water of the Black Army's fight against the Bolsheviks to the east. Firing his old bolt-action at those horses. Budyonny headed the charge, and he was thrown off his horse when a stray bullet hit the brute's torso. As the Black Army beat off the Reds. At the end of it all, Siuda shot Budyonny in the head. The news carried throughout the region. The devil of Boguchany was dead. Why then, Pyodor thought, was some anonymous soldier executing Budyonny, and not Pyotr? It took a moment, but it dawned on Pyodor. Stepanov, that old bastard, wasn't trying to trumpet Pyotr's achievements. He was trying to trumpet the Black Army's. No better than Bukharin.
strings.SBA_Despotist.22.a: One day, we'll use them to wipe our asses.
strings.SBA_Despotist.23.desc:
“Put Mishurenko on the line.” Ivan Stepanov barked the orders from his bed, impatiently waiting for whatever idiot was working in Mishurenko's office that day to patch him through. He looked up to the tremendous, white marble, ceiling of his bedroom. He had it recently renovated at the expense of Kilchichakov. The leech he was, the way money disappeared from the budget in his presence would impress Stepanov if it weren't so tedious.

“Comrade Stepanov, this is Androniy Mishurenko.” Stepanov could hear the spit flying out of his mouth. How on Earth did he ever end up with this man as his most trusted advisor?

“Is Yevgeniya with you? She mentioned she would be stopping by your office. Something about a-”

“The terrorist attack in Kansk? Yes I am familiar.”

Stepanov was taken aback. When did Mishuernko grow a pair of balls? He resisted the urge to tear him a new asshole, business came first. “Is she down there or not?”

“No. She never came by.” Silence. “Comrade Stepanov, have you heard about them?”

The line pushed him over the edge, “Cut the cryptic bullshit, dear God. I thought I had the last of that with Siuda, for fuck's sake.” Silence once more. Stepanov bit his lip, he did really want to know... “Tell me what's going on, Androniy. Do I need to come to Kansk?”
strings.SBA_Despotist.23.a: “I would stay out of the city if I were you.”
strings.SBA_Despotist.24.desc:
Andrey groaned as he lay down in his bed, his body aching from his latest confrontation. Some local factory workers had decided to vandalize Andrey's home, and later had cornered him and beat him bloody. Maksim was still working his shift in the munitions factory, and Andrey hoped he wouldn't get too worried when he saw him. Maksim had it hard enough normally, Andrey didn't want to put even more of a burden on him. He had even gone through the trouble to clean the paint off the door, even if he was so sore the old lady next door had to help him carry the water.

Andrey remembered a time when this kind of thing wouldn't happen. Sure, things weren't perfect, but if things got bad you could go to some soldiers and get the bigots to at least apologize. When he was getting beaten, he was pretty sure he recognized one of the soldiers he had notified amongst the thugs. Maybe it was the head trauma, but Andrey couldn't remember when things changed. The shift in attitude happened after the Security Council took charge, but they had been some of the proponents of the protections, right?

Andrey sighed. Just a few more days and he'd go back to his unit, who were more accepting. Andrey, ironically, was the lucky one, even if he didn't particularly feel like it right now.
strings.SBA_Despotist.24.a: You never know what you truly had until it's gone.
strings.SBA_general_assembly_category_desc: The communes of the Free Territory form the 'General Assembly', a de-facto legislative body for our glorious society. Here, the grievances and ideas of the communes can be heard and collective decisions made for the benefit of all free peoples of the world. Naturally we are free of the corrupt dealings and tit-for-tat of bourgeois 'democracies', and any appearance of such is a simple misinterpretation of anarchist methods.
strings.SBA_general_assembly_information_tt:
Votes can be held on a variety of issues through the “Show Motions” button. There are three types of issues that can be addressed: Reforms, Resolutions, and Motions.

Reforms will provide permanent changes to the effects of the national spirit “The Siberian Free Territory”. They can only be voted on once the prerequisite reform has been passed and they have been unlocked through a national focus.

Resolutions affect the policies upheld by the General Assembly and Security Council. They can only be voted on once they have been unlocked through a national focus or event.

Motions are less impactful, and will provide smaller bonuses to the Free Territory. After a motion has been proposed, it cannot be proposed again for 180 days.

Issues will be debated in the General Assembly for a period of 60 days. If two-thirds of the communal representatives vote in favour of the issue, it will be passed.

Each Commune has a set of ethos that will influence how they will vote on different issues. Communes can be swayed to support an issue through concessions.

strings.SBA_power_struggle_category_desc:
The tensions within the Free Territory between the General Assembly and the Security Council have erupted into a full power struggle. Pyotr Siuda and Ivan Stepanov, the two most powerful figures in Central Siberia, jockey for influence in our nascent experiment; their conflicting beliefs of idealism and pragmatism will be pitted against each other in the colosseum of the Far East, where each man is gathering support in preparation for the final showdown in Novosibirsk.

In the absence of the Free Territory's most notable leaders and as the Assembly's deputies and Council's commanders bicker without end, it has fallen on the Black Army and its rank-and-file soldiers to maintain order - as much as order can be maintained in an anarchist society, that is.

strings.SBA_build_a_nuke_workshop_desc:
The quest for nuclear weaponry is one that every aspiring power must undertake before cementing themselves as a lead role on the world stage.

While many nations undertake this quest from inside their laboratories, testing weapons on islands, and threatening the nations of the world with nuclear armageddon, the Free Territory has chosen a different route. Under the guidance of Pyotr Siuda the people of Russia will assert themselves as a force to be reckoned with. To maintain Protect EMANSIPATSIYA's goal of building an atom bomb with the people's help, Pyotr Siuda will travel from commune to commune, asking for the people's input. With the millions of people in Siberia, comes millions of differing opinions. Choosing between which advice to take and which to disregard will decide the fate of Protect EMANSIPATSIYA and Russia at large.
